Code wordPlain meaning
Screen / composableWhat the user sees inside a Compose UI.
ActivityAn Android window or entry point; not every feature has its own Activity.
ViewModel / sessionThe current screen/conversation state and operations.
Repository / managerThe owner or coordinator used to read and update shared data.
DAO / database / entityQueries, storage schema and stored record shape.
Service / receiver / workerBackground lifetime, event/alarm delivery and deferred work.
Parser / executorInterpret input / apply a validated action. These are different responsibilities.
Asset / resourcePackaged text, art, fonts, layouts or static data; these do not all share one license.

02 / Where things appear

The UI tree

This is an explanation of the existing app, not a proposed redesign. Route names are included because some do not match what you see.

Visible destinationCode / internal route

TodosTodosScreen.kt · todos

Other surfaces

Habits and Routines are secondary pages; Screen Time has its own route. Floating chat and widget configuration are Android entry points outside the ordinary bottom-dock pages. Note sharing/quick edit, drills, voice capture, chest reveal and backup dialogs are focused flows or overlays.

03 / Structure

How the code fits together

The folder tree is about responsibilities, not an instruction to reorganize files. Several features intentionally cross folders: widgets use note/task repositories, and chat executes the same actions as the native pages.

Ayva/                                 Repository (product: RUN)
├── app/src/main/
│   ├── java/com/focusbyrj/app/
│   │   ├── FocusApplication.kt        Startup and shared owners
│   │   ├── MainActivity.kt            Routes and main window
│   │   ├── ui/                        Screens, components, theme, speech
│   │   ├── data/                      Models, DAOs, repositories, databases
│   │   ├── util/assistant/            Context, language, planning, experiences
│   │   ├── util/backup/ + crypto/     Recovery, encryption, data boundaries
│   │   ├── service/                   Alarms, background service, overlays
│   │   └── widget/                    Launcher renderers, actions, editors
│   ├── assets/                        Dictionary, seed data, animation, rules
│   ├── res/                           Fonts, drawables, raw scenes, layouts
│   ├── jniLibs/                       Packaged native worker by CPU ABI
│   └── AndroidManifest.xml            Android components and permissions
├── app/schemas/                       Exported Room migration evidence
├── app/src/test/ + androidTest/       Host regression and device checks
├── tools/                             Importers, generators, native build, checks
├── gradle/ + *.gradle.kts              Dependencies and Android build rules
├── .github/workflows/                 Validation and release automation
├── fastlane/metadata/                 Store listing text and graphics
├── docs/                              Plans, audit history, design evidence
└── LICENSE + TRADEMARK.md             Source grant and separate brand policy

The shared-owner rule

A screen, chat message and widget can be three ways to operate on one task. Their UI state may differ, but they should not become three competing task databases. Look for the repository or canonical owner when changing behavior.

Feature 01 / 13

Find your way around

One activity hosts the main pages; Android entry points also open focused tools.

What you see

The bottom dock has Focus, Todos, Notes, a blank placeholder, and Profile. Habits, Routines, Screen Time and Settings are secondary destinations. Chat can also open as its own floating window.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • Startup recovery completes before ordinary data managers start.
  • MainActivity supplies the repositories and ViewModels used by the visible screens.
  • The top-bar profile/avatar shortcut and the bottom Profile button have different destinations: Preferences versus Account.

Screen.ktRoute-name registry. The route named empty opens Notes; empty_tab is the blank placeholder.
FocusBottomBar.ktFive-slot bottom dock. Its fourth slot is a blank placeholder; Habits and Routines are reached elsewhere.

AyvaIcon.ktAyva Icon component in app shell & navigation.

When changing this: The internal name empty means Notes; empty_tab is the actual blank tab. Twelve launcher aliases are alternative icons for the same app, not twelve apps or screens.

Material / infrastructure: Project navigation and manifest; UI uses AndroidX Compose and Material libraries.

Feature 02 / 13

Focus, app blocking & routines

Turn a focus session or recurring rule into the right blocking window.

What you see

Home focus controls, installed-app categories and restrictions, routine schedules, temporary access and Screen Time statistics. Hard/soft blocking windows appear over restricted apps.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • Restrictions and routines live in FocusDatabase; usage observations come from Android Usage Access.
  • The foreground service evaluates restrictions and directly adds WindowManager overlay views.
  • Timer end alarms, boot recovery and screen on/off handling keep the service independent of the visible page.

Feature 03 / 13

Tasks, dates & reminders

One task record powers the list, assistant commands, reminders and widgets.

What you see

Todos, quick add, recurring work, task dependencies/checklists and planned work sessions. The same task can be shown in chat or a home-screen widget.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • SmartDateParser extracts supported dates; the surrounding conversation or screen decides what the date belongs to.

Feature 05 / 13

Notes, editor & attachments

Edit rich notes and safely connect their text, blocks and encrypted media.

What you see

Notes grid, labels, checklists, rich text, tables, sketches, image collages, audio memos, archive/private vault, sharing and PDF/DOCX exports.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • Editor widgets transform note content; the ViewModel and repository persist the model.
  • NoteDatabase is SQLCipher-backed. Attachments are separate encrypted files referenced by the note.

Feature 06 / 13

Vault, backup & recovery

Keep local protection, portable backups and crash recovery distinct.

What you see

Private notes vault, encrypted export/restore/verify, safety snapshots, saved drafts, recovery phrase and storage tools.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • Portable backups use a password-derived key; internal snapshots and local media use device-held keys. They solve different problems.
  • Restore validates and stages material before replacing live data; a journal supports interrupted-operation recovery.
  • FocusApplication runs pending recovery before starting ordinary writers. Participating writers use the maintenance gate.

Feature 07 / 13

Chat, Plan, Talk & offline experiences

Use bounded offline features and route real actions through shared app data owners.

What you see

Floating bubble/chat, Chat/Plan/Talk/Drill modes, task and habit actions, trip checklists, saved plans, dictionary, discovery, word games, riddles, jokes, facts and stories.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • The composer and mode select a supported intent; session context carries pending references and edits.
  • Planning maintains draft/workspace state, then guarded executors apply changes to canonical tasks with receipts/undo. The existing planning behavior is not changed by this guide.
  • The chat three-dot menu opens a bubble-icon picker using the same 12 app-icon assets. It stores the bubble choice separately and updates the existing overlay without restarting the service.
  • Finite experiences and content rotation are separate from open-ended dialogue. Rotation preferences survive clearing chat. Dictionary definitions come from Wordset shards.
  • Optional native ChatScript runs in a crash-isolated worker and has a Kotlin fallback. It is not an unrestricted language model.

Feature 08 / 13

Voice capture & transcript editing

Turn a recognizer session into editable text before the assistant acts.

What you see

Speech popup, live visualization, styles and editable transcription. Notes audio recording is a separate feature.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • The popup projects partial/final recognized text and allows correction before submission.

  • A note audio memo records audio for attachment storage; that is not the same operation as speech-to-text.

Feature 10 / 13

Profile, economy, quests & Pro

Present progress and rewards without letting animation decide the award.

What you see

Profile/avatar/bio, gold, level, activity/streak matrix, achievements, habit telemetry, pinned notes, shortcuts, daily quests, mystery boxes and lifetime Pro.

Responsibility tour. Arrows show how these concerns connect; they do not assert that each file directly calls the next.

How the parts help each other

  • Profile aggregates several owners: economy, streaks, habits, notes and local settings. It is not one new database of copies.
  • DailyQuestManager resolves an award; the chest dialog presents that result. Skip ends presentation, not reward calculation.

04 / What connects to what

Follow an action through RUN

These are cross-feature responsibility sequences. They show why changing one small parser, file format or UI action can affect multiple surfaces. They are not packet captures or traces from a live device.

This map highlights selected shared owners and consumers. It is not an exhaustive execution graph.

1. “Plan a Goa trip on the 26th” → a real task

01 →User text + selected mode
02 →Date/intent + conversation context
03 →Draft main task + subtasks
04 →Edit / remove / summarize / finalize
05 →Guarded action + receipt
06 →TaskRepository → FocusDatabase
07 →List + reminders + widgets

Dates and checklist items belong to a draft until the supported finalization/action path applies them. A summary reads state; it must not become another task. Editing a date must update the same task and reminder schedule. The archive/receipts support revisiting work without creating a parallel task authority.

Trace in: OfflineAssistant.kt · AssistantSession.kt · TripChecklistConversation.kt · PlanTemporalLanguage.kt · AssistantActionExecutor.kt · CanonicalPlanTasks.kt · TaskRepository.kt

2. Add an image → show it in a note

01 →Picker or shared input
02 →Import checks + bounded decoding
03 →Encrypted attachment file
04 →Note stores media reference
05 →EncryptedMediaFetcher decrypts
06 →Coil / editor renders image

The image bytes and note record are separate. Both references and bytes must survive backup/restore. Export deliberately decrypts into a user-requested artifact and needs cleanup; editor display alone should use the encrypted-media fetch path.

Trace in: ShareToNoteActivity.kt · NoteImageHelper.kt · NoteMediaManager.kt · EncryptedMediaStorage.kt · NoteEntity.kt · EncryptedMediaFetcher.kt

3. Restore a backup → recover safely after interruption

01 →Pick file + enter password
02 →Parse bounds / authenticate / validate
03 →Stage databases + media
04 →Journal + maintenance coordination
05 →Apply live state / rebuild references
06 →Reload caches / rebind local IDs

An interrupted restore is a recoverable operation, not just a single copy command. Startup checks the journal before managers resume ordinary writes. Database keys, media encryption and launcher widget IDs cannot simply be copied as if all were portable identifiers.

Trace in: CryptoBackupEngine.kt · BackupRestoreManager.kt · RestoreStaging.kt · RestoreJournal.kt · MaintenanceGate.kt · FocusApplication.kt

4. A reminder becomes due while RUN is hidden

01 →Repository’s current record
02 →Alarm / WorkManager schedule
03 →Receiver revalidates eligibility
04 →Notification + queued overlay
05 →User action through shared owner
06 →Cancel / reschedule / reconcile

Notifications, overlays and foreground-service indicators have different identities and lifetimes. Pause, deletion, completion or a date change invalidates stale work. Boot/time change rebuilds eligible work; it must not reactivate a disabled bubble feature.

Trace in: TaskReminderHelper.kt · TaskReminderReceiver.kt · TaskNotifications.kt · UnifiedOverlayCoordinator.kt · HabitAlarmScheduler.kt · BootReceiver.kt

5. Look up a word → save a learning sense

01 →Supported lookup intent
02 →Normalize / hash word
03 →Read matching compressed shard
04 →Select actual sense + credits
05 →Bookmark / link vocabulary
06 →Native learning quiz/progress

The app does not load a language model or unpack the whole dictionary at startup. Wordset definitions, sense-specific editorial examples and legacy vocabulary are separate sources. Saving a sense does not create a note or mark it learned.

Trace in: AssistantDictionary.kt · AssistantDictionaryStore.kt · AssistantVocabularyFeatures.kt · VocabRepository.kt · VocabDatabase.kt

6. Open a mystery box → collect exactly one award

01 →Quest eligibility / completion
02 →Resolve reward once
03 →Persist reward state
04 →Choose tier’s visual scene
05 →Reveal / skip presentation
06 →Collect existing result

The animation is presentation. Common, Rare, Epic and Legendary share Smoke Paw artwork with different visual intensity/colors. Skipping, replaying or lifecycle changes must not calculate a new reward.

Trace in: DailyQuestManager.kt · FocusEconomyManager.kt · DuolingoMysteryChestDialog.kt · SmokePawChestScene.kt

05 / The protection map

Data stores, keys & recovery

There is no single “the app is encrypted” switch. Database encryption, private-note locking, local media protection and portable backups protect different material with different keys.

StoreFormat / protectionContent and key boundary
FocusDatabaseSQLCipher-backed Room • schema 16Tasks, routines, restrictions, habits/logs and assistant receipts

DatabaseKeyProvider wraps the database passphrase using AndroidKeyStore.
Primary productivity store; change migrations and all consumers together.
NoteDatabaseSQLCipher-backed Room • schema 7Note records, block/text state, labels and media references

DatabaseKeyProvider protects the SQLCipher passphrase; private payload has another vault layer.
Original attachment bytes are separate files, not contained in every note row.
Encrypted attachmentsAES-GCM filesOriginal note media and audio references

Device-held media master key; legacy input handling separate.
Device-bound encryption must be converted appropriately for portable backup.
Private archived payloadVault subkey / encrypted payloadPrivate archived note contents

Stable vault data key wrapped with PIN-derived key; recovery flow separate.
Vault PIN is not the entire app lock or portable backup password.
Assistant protected state / snapshotsAYSN1 device-key envelopeInternal snapshots, assistant workspace/session state as used by callers

SnapshotCryptoEngine + AndroidKeyStore-held key.
Device-key files are not a portable recovery plan after uninstall/key loss.
AyvaChatDatabaseApp-private Room SQLite • schema 1Chat messages and active drill state

No SQLCipher delegate configured in this database builder.
App-private does not mean world-readable; do not claim extra app-level encryption here.
DrillDatabaseApp-private Room SQLite • schema 1Drill session summaries/progress records

No SQLCipher delegate configured here.
Separate from the encrypted Focus/Notes databases.
VocabDatabaseApp-private Room SQLite • schema 3Legacy seed + user vocabulary/bookmarks/progress

Room seed asset and migrations; no SQLCipher delegate configured here.
Replacing the seed for rights reasons must preserve user learning state.
Preferences & local bindingsAndroid app-private preferences/filesTheme, settings, widget style/IDs, rotation counters and feature flags

Protection varies by owner; not one universal encrypted preference store.
A settings reset, chat clear and restore have different intended scopes.
Portable encrypted backupPassword envelope • current format 4Supported exported records/media assembled by BackupRestoreManager

Argon2id 64 MB, t=3, p=1 + AES-256-GCM; legacy readers retained.
Portable with the correct password. Verify actual restore coverage, not just successful decryption.

Before uninstalling or switching distribution certificates: make and verify a portable password backup. Device-bound internal snapshots are not enough. KeyStore key availability/hardware backing varies by device, and neither this diagram nor successful decryption proves every restore flow is correct.

Where data leaves a protection boundary

  • User-requested PDF/DOCX/share output can be plaintext and needs a scoped temporary-file lease and cleanup.
  • The Android speech provider may process audio outside RUN, including on its own network connection.
  • A widget exposes only its configured content on the home screen; style config and source note/task records have different owners.
  • Diagnostics/backup content must be reviewed for what it contains before sharing; a file being inside the app sandbox is not an encryption claim.
06 / Provenance & license map

What came from where?

Borrowing can mean code, a dataset, a font, a player library or the art it plays. Each needs its own evidence.

Evidence labels: “Confirmed shipped” means a matching runtime asset/build path is present. “Project-declared” is documentation or an ownership statement. “Unknown” means rights/source evidence is missing. “Research only” is not evidence of incorporation. These labels do not accuse anyone of copying.

Confirmed shipped data

Wordset dictionary

app/src/main/assets/dictionary/ • tools/import_dictionary.py

Evidence: Wordset commit 4503bfafbe4556361a296b9d368c18168dfb56c3; docs/assistant/DICTIONARY_DATA.md

Terms / limit: CC BY-SA 4.0 plus retained WordNet notice. Preserve contributors, links and change labels; adapted data stays under the same license.

Practical next step: Keep; complete data/source/credits chain already documented.

Confirmed shipped native component

ChatScript / WordNet / LLVM

jniLibs/*/librun_dialogue.so • assets/conversation/native-v1.* • tools/experiments/chatscript/

Evidence: ChatScript commit 9f5eec4736ba22bd992a6498c1e0052e2a795125; source patch, worker and packaging scripts; bundled notices

Terms / limit: ChatScript MIT; component WordNet/LLVM notices. App-authored rule pack has its own project provenance.

Practical next step: Keep functionality; add a source-build recipe rather than relying on checked-in .so or binary archive.

Known provenance gap

Legacy vocabulary seed

app/src/main/assets/vocab.db

Evidence: DICTIONARY_DATA.md explicitly records missing source documentation for 1,773 idioms and 2,027 OWS entries.

Terms / limit: No separate license established. Wordset’s license does not cover this seed.

Practical next step: Recover source/permission or replace the bundled seed; preserve user learning data through migration.

Downloaded art; item terms unknown

20 dotLottie files + raw cat JSON

app/src/main/assets/*.lottie • res/raw/cat_animation.json

Evidence: Creator/download URL and license version generally absent. Generic LottieFiles manifest author is not item-level evidence.

Terms / limit: Lottie runtime Apache 2.0 is separate. Simple License permits redistribution subject to its conditions, including an asset-service restriction; exact item/date terms must be matched.

Practical next step: Recover each page/license; if redistributable but not FLOSS, discuss NonFreeAssets with F-Droid or replace art.

Downloaded art; item terms unknown

6 Rive cat files

app/src/main/assets/*.riv

Evidence: Original item/creator records need recovery.

Terms / limit: Current public Rive Community Content is CC BY 4.0 under Rive terms C.6; private/premium items can differ. Runtime MIT is separate.

Practical next step: Verify qualifying public source; provide creator, source, license and modification credits, or replace unresolved items.

Embedded license evidence

Bundled fonts

app/src/main/res/font/*.ttf

Evidence: Name-table copyright and license fields extracted in the file inspector. Allura OFL additionally bundled.

Terms / limit: Caveat, Nunito, Roboto Mono, Roboto Serif, Allura: OFL markers. Roboto Slab: Apache 2.0 marker. Match actual file and retain full required notices.

Practical next step: Keep when evidence/notice chain complete; enumerate authors and license text in third-party credits.

Project source and artwork pipeline

Vizag scenes / Smoke Paw chest

tools/vizag_replacements/ • res/raw/vizag_* • assets/smoke_paw_chest.html

Evidence: Approved source image, scene paths and export code; chest design notes. Bare Browser was an inspiration in the conversation.

Terms / limit: Project-wide AGPL declaration is not an independent audit of every artistic contribution. Source/ownership should be recorded.

Practical next step: Keep exact current art; document authorship, generation/edit history and rights for distribution. No proof established of copied Bare Browser SVG.

Project content; verify per item

Stories, facts, games, quotations

ExperienceContent.kt • EntertainmentPack.kt • ConversationStories.kt • FocusQuotes.kt • SummaryQuotes.kt

Evidence: Docs identify original retellings and short fact wording with references; traditional plots are not a license for a modern retelling.

Terms / limit: Do not infer all quotations or knowledge-base text are public domain. Review attribution, source and exact expression.

Practical next step: Retain original retellings; build a per-content source list; replace any copied modern text without adequate rights.

Influence or naming; copying unestablished

Notesnook / Duolingo names

Notesnook*.kt • Duolingo*.kt

Evidence: A class/file name is insufficient evidence of a copied upstream implementation.

Terms / limit: If a real port is identified, record original file, commit, changes and compatible terms; do not invent attribution from names.

Practical next step: Inspect git history and actual source similarity before categorizing as borrowed code.

Research only unless matched to runtime

Research candidate repositories

docs/assistant/research/

Evidence: A reviewed project appearing in research notes is not a dependency declaration or proof of bundled code.

Terms / limit: Apply licenses only to content actually incorporated. GitHub public visibility alone grants no reuse license.

Practical next step: Separate candidate list from shipped-material ledger.

Declared supporting libraries

Gradle libraries & icons

app/build.gradle.kts • gradle/libs.versions.toml

Evidence: Pinned direct dependencies; resolved transitive components depend on the actual build.

Terms / limit: Mostly Apache 2.0/MIT/BSD/OFL families; exact version, transitive and NOTICE obligations still matter.

Practical next step: Keep FLOSS libraries; consolidate notices excluded by packaging and verify the final APK.

Project declarations conflict in places

RUN source / name / logo

LICENSE • README.md • TRADEMARK.md • 135 production Kotlin headers

Evidence: Root declares AGPLv3; restrictive proprietary/confidential headers persist. Trademark text explicitly calls for F-Droid permission.

Terms / limit: Rights holder must clarify the effective grant and authorize distribution of the name/icon. Trademark rights and source copyright are different.

Practical next step: Reconcile owned-source headers; record F-Droid brand authorization without abandoning the brand.

09 / Concrete preparation plan

F-Droid: change what to what

A plausible route to F-Droid exists. The current checkout is not submission-ready with confidence.

The work is mainly evidence, source-build integration, rights consistency and accurate distribution metadata. App blocking, encryption, Android 12+ support and local Pro verification do not by themselves require removal. No application changes were made for this report.

1 — establish rights

01 · Source licensing

Current
Root AGPLv3 alongside 135 production files with explicit proprietary/confidential restrictions.

Required / intended target
A consistent free-software grant for the code actually shipped; compatible third-party grants retained.

Where: LICENSE; README.md; per-file headers in RUN-file-index.csv; imported-source records.

Effect on the app: No feature removal needed. Only the rightsholder can clarify owned-code grants; third-party restrictions cannot be waived by the app owner.

Acceptance evidence: Review all restrictive headers, keep copyright authors, run license checks and resolve exceptions.

1 — establish rights

02 · Name/icon permission

Current
TRADEMARK.md separately requires written permission for F-Droid distribution with RUN branding.

Required / intended target
Explicit authorization covering F-Droid’s permitted builds/distribution, or a deliberately rebranded distribution.

Where: TRADEMARK.md and F-Droid submission discussion.

Effect on the app: Authorization can keep RUN branding and applicationId. Fork-renaming rules need not be applied to an authorized official distribution.

Acceptance evidence: Ensure the authorization is public, unambiguous and compatible with the planned signing/build arrangement.

1 — establish rights

03 · Downloaded art & legacy text

Current
26 animation files lack a complete item source/terms ledger; legacy vocab.db provenance missing. Raw cat JSON, quotes, images and knowledge text need a rights sweep.

Required / intended target
For each item: author + original URL + license/version + changes + required notices. Replace only unresolved/non-redistributable items.

Where: assets/*.lottie; assets/*.riv; assets/vocab.db; res/raw; content Kotlin/JSON; asset ledger.

Effect on the app: Do not delete user notes or vocabulary progress. Alternative art can preserve the feature; seed replacement needs stable-ID migration.

Acceptance evidence: Match the actual binary/data to source evidence. Generic “free download” or engine license is insufficient.

2 — reproducible source

04 · Native dialogue build

Current
Four checked-in librun_dialogue.so files plus generated native-v1.zip; Gradle does not rebuild them from the pinned upstream source.

Required / intended target
F-Droid metadata builds the supported native worker from pinned ChatScript + tracked patch/wrapper and recreates rule artifacts/hashes.

Where: tools/experiments/chatscript/{build_android.py,restricted.patch,worker.cpp,package_runtime.py}; app/src/main/jniLibs; assets/conversation.

Effect on the app: Keep native dialogue and its Kotlin fallback. Build coverage must match the ABIs promised by the distribution; non-shipping placeholders need explicit handling.

Acceptance evidence: Clean checkout without prebuilt .so; verify pinned source/NDK; run smoke/worker checks; inspect APK; use scanner and recipe review. Do not blindly ignore binaries.

2 — notices

05 · Third-party credit delivery

Current
Gradle excludes several LICENSE/NOTICE resources. Some notices are bundled, but an exact final-APK notice inventory is incomplete.

Required / intended target
Consolidated third-party notices/assets credits reachable in the app and retained in source/artifacts as required.

Where: app/build.gradle.kts packaging resources; assets/licenses; dictionary/LICENSE.txt; Help/about.

Effect on the app: Small text addition; no need to replace good libraries merely to remove notice obligations.

Acceptance evidence: Compare final dependency graph and bundled assets with notices; include SQLCipher, Argon2Kt, Rive/Lottie, fonts and transitive requirements.

3 — build & metadata

06 · F-Droid recipe

Current
GitHub Actions builds/signs a single Android 12+ release APK; no F-Droid recipe demonstrated.

Required / intended target
An accepted fdroiddata recipe with source revision, Gradle/SDK/NDK settings, binary handling and accurate versions/metadata.

Where: New metadata/com.focusbyrj.app.yml in fdroiddata; app/build.gradle.kts; .github/workflows; source-generation scripts.

Effect on the app: Existing GitHub release can remain. Normal FLOSS Maven dependencies are not equivalent to unexplained checked-in executable blobs.

Acceptance evidence: Run fdroid scanner/build in the F-Droid environment. This guide has not run an official F-Droid build and cannot guarantee approval.

3 — build & metadata

07 · Privacy & feature descriptions

Current
No RUN INTERNET permission; SpeechRecognizer uses the default provider. Fastlane still mentions battery-health statistics after removal.

Required / intended target
Describe core offline operation, optional provider-dependent speech, real permission reasons and current features accurately.

Where: OnDeviceTranscriber.kt; SpeechServiceDiagnostics.kt; AndroidManifest.xml; README.md; fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/full_description.txt.

Effect on the app: Keep voice as optional provider integration. An offline-capable provider may be chosen; do not silently promise offline recognition on all phones.

Acceptance evidence: Check merged manifest, provider/network behavior and storefront text. Declare applicable anti-features honestly with maintainers.

3 — distribution decision

08 · Art anti-feature

Current
Some art may permit redistribution while imposing conditions that are not fully free-software compatible.

Required / intended target
Use FLOSS art, or if policy permits the exact redistributable non-free art, mark NonFreeAssets; no non-free runtime code.

Where: Animation/license ledger; source credits; F-Droid metadata.

Effect on the app: NonFreeAssets is distinct from non-free SDKs. Current policy allows some redistributable non-free assets; not all asset uncertainty means rejection.

Acceptance evidence: Show actual item license to maintainers. Rive public CC BY 4.0 and Lottie Simple License are different cases.

4 — protect users

09 · Signing & migration

Current
Existing installs use the GitHub release certificate. A different signing key cannot replace that install in place.

Required / intended target
Choose reproducible upstream-signature verification/copying if accepted, or plan a safe explicit distribution migration.

Where: Release signing/build settings; F-Droid reproducibility metadata; portable backup/restore UX.

Effect on the app: Do not share private signing keys. Avoid instructing users to uninstall before verified portable backup; device-key snapshots do not survive key loss.

Acceptance evidence: Install/update on a separate test device; test password backup restore, notes/media/vault, tasks and widget rebind. Document certificate ownership.

4 — submission

10 · Eligibility & review

Current
Initial source history is 19 Sep 2026; assessment is 3 Nov 2026. Public maturity is under the usual three-month guideline.

Required / intended target
Demonstrate the app has users/qualifies for the documented exception, or meet normal maturity; submit complete evidence.

Where: Public repository history; submission issue; build metadata and screenshots.

Effect on the app: No need to weaken encryption, remove app blocking, drop Android 12+, or automatically remove local Pro unlocking.

Acceptance evidence: Maintainers decide inclusion. Policy, scanners and dependency signatures can change after this dated snapshot.

A safe order

  • Resolve code/brand rights and material provenance first; classify actual assets rather than removing whole features.
  • Build the native worker/rule pack from pinned source and consolidate exact notices.
  • Prepare the F-Droid recipe, accurate metadata/anti-features and signing strategy.
  • Prove clean builds and safe update/backup/restore on test devices, then submit for maintainer review.

F-Droid makes the final inclusion decision. This is a dated code/policy assessment, not an official acceptance review, successful F-Droid build or legal opinion. A NonFreeAssets declaration does not cure missing redistribution permission.

10 / Delivery map

Build, release & distribution

The current GitHub release path produces one universal APK for Android 12+; CPU-specific native libraries inside it do not mean separate apps. Compile/target SDK is 35 and minSdk is 31 in this checkout.

FilePurpose
build.gradle.ktsAndroid version, min/target SDK, shrinking, packaging, dependencies and conditional signing.
libs.versions.tomlLibrary/plugin version catalog.
validate.ymlRuns boundary/dictionary checks, unit tests and unsigned builds on changes/PRs.
release.ymlBuilds/tests, conditionally signs, prepares one universal APK, publishes only when release intent permits.
release_intent.pyDistinguishes an intended release/retry from a change that should not publish a duplicate version.
package_release_apks.pyChecks that release output is a single universal APK, names it and writes checksums/manifest.
proguard-rules.proRelease shrinker keep rules for reflection, serialization and Android/native integration.
settings.gradle.ktsRepository/plugin/dependency-resolution setup.

Three separate questions

  • Does it compile and pass the chosen checks? That is build correctness.
  • Can another builder recreate the eligible artifact from approved source? That is the source/reproducibility question.
  • Can that artifact update an existing install with its certificate? That is Android signing compatibility.
11 / Avoid feature conflicts

Before you change something

Use this as a starting checklist before changing a feature. It shows consumers worth inspecting; it is not a demand to rewrite working code.

If you change…Start in…Also verify…
Bubble icon / shared app artworkBubbleIconManager.kt • BubbleIconPicker.kt • BubbleService.ktUse existing app icons, retain selected ID, refresh an existing overlay, preserve snooze/disabled state, and match the docking preview.
Bottom Profile destinationMainActivity.kt • FocusBottomBar.kt • Screen.ktDock tap, back stack, top avatar → Settings, return from settings.
Task or plan date behaviorSmartDateParser.kt + caller in assistant/task UI + TaskRepositorySame-turn date, later correction, summary, removal, recurrence, reminder and widget agreement.
Note schema / block serializationNoteEntity.kt • NoteDatabase.kt • RichTextEngine.kt • NotesnookBlockModel.ktOld notes, tables/checklists, media references, export, backup and widget display.
Media import/exportNoteImageHelper.kt • NoteMediaManager.kt • EncryptedMediaStorage.kt • ArticleExporter.ktOversized/corrupt input, cancellation, temp leases, private-vault display, backup byte integrity.
Encryption or restoreCryptoBackupEngine.kt • BackupRestoreManager.kt • RestoreJournal.kt • DatabaseKeyProvider.ktWrong password, tampering, legacy formats, interrupted commit, restart recovery and data retention.
Habit pauseHabitPause.kt • HabitRepository.kt • HabitAlarmScheduler.kt • assistant habit editingIntervals, resume, midnight/timezone, paused denominator, shield/streak calculations and stale notifications.
Bubble visibilityBubbleService.kt • BubbleSettingsScreen.kt • BootReceiver.ktDisable vs snooze, ten-minute return when enabled, landscape hide, screen off/on and stale restart.
Widget font/editorNoteWidgetTypography.kt • Provider/Service • config ActivitiesNew/existing widget, note switch, resize, launcher recreation, font scale and Apply persistence.
Game/story rotationChatExperiences.kt • content files • rotation preferencesClear chat, restart, category choices, next/hint/answer, no repeated fixed first item.
New downloaded artworkassets/res + renderer + provenance ledgerExact source/creator/license, app credit, reduced motion, light/dark, lifecycle and byte budget.
Native dialogue versionbuild_android.py • restricted.patch • package_runtime.py • NativeGeneralDialogue.ktPinned source/ABI, restricted capability checks, crash fallback, zip digest and source-build reproducibility.
Settings or storefront copySettingsSearchCatalog.kt • SettingsDestinations.kt • fastlane/metadataSearch aliases, sensitive routes, removed battery/DND claims, recognizer privacy and screenshots.

Permission boundaries worth remembering

Permission / capabilityWhat it connects to
SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOWBlocking/reminder/chat overlays; user-controlled special access.
PACKAGE_USAGE_STATSForeground-app and Screen Time observations; user-granted usage access.
POST_NOTIFICATIONSReminder/service notification visibility on supported Android versions.
SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM / USE_EXACT_ALARMTime-sensitive scheduling declarations/availability; inspect actual manifest and device policy.
RECORD_AUDIOMicrophone capture for selected voice/audio features.
CAMERAUser-triggered QR/camera flow where available.
FOREGROUND_SERVICE familiesDeclared long-running Android service types and platform restrictions.
INTERNETExplicitly removed from RUN manifest; external speech provider is a separate boundary.

Capabilities above explain feature relationships, not a claim every named scheduling variant is requested. The interactive inspector includes the exact declared permissions and removed entries from AndroidManifest.xml; merged manifest and Android-version policy govern runtime availability.

How to use the evidence

  • Open the test source and extracted method list in the file inspector to see the scenario and assertions. A filename such as SecurityAuditTest is not a formal security certification.
  • Unit/Robolectric checks can exercise rules, serialization and many UI cases. Physical-device checks are still needed for KeyStore, OEM scheduling, speech providers, launchers and overlay lifetime.
  • Historical docs and reports are checkpoints. They may mention removed features or old layouts; current code and the pinned revision define this atlas.
  • For a future release, run the relevant unit checks, then targeted device flows and source/asset validation. Do not interpret an old green report as validation of a new build.

How this atlas was verified

Every git-tracked file is counted once and hashed. Reviewed feature paths are checked to resolve to real files. Static source references and methods are indexed with their extraction limits. The final HTML is tested without network access; the PDF is checked for readable text, links and representative rendered pages. Validation details are included in atlas-validation.json.

Appendix B / Read before making claims

Sources, scope & handover

This atlas describes commit cce930915554c64c4884b134c238daed93e78155 and version 2.0.37. It inventories tracked source, resources, assets, tests and tools. Build outputs, local signing credentials, user data, caches and existing untracked mockups are excluded. No private keys, secrets or real user databases are copied into the guide.

What this guide does and does not establish

  • The inventory is complete for git-tracked files at this snapshot. Reviewed diagrams explain architecture; long-tail file roles and static coupling are extracted/inferred and labelled. Reflection, dynamic dispatch, generated code, resource lookup and runtime-only relationships can be missing from static edges.
  • A matching upstream notice and pinned source provide stronger origin evidence than a filename or prior research plan. Unknown material is explicitly left unknown; direct copying of Notesnook/Duolingo/Bare Browser is not established here.
  • License family summaries are preparation guidance. This is not a legal opinion, an exhaustive source-similarity audit, a complete release-APK SBOM or an official F-Droid acceptance decision.
  • Primary policy pages were reviewed for this assessment; terms and scanners can change. Item-specific historical download terms may differ from current website terms.
  • Historical screenshots/docs are labelled and may differ from device state. Generating this atlas does not redesign app screens or change app behavior.

Primary external sources

  1. F-Droid inclusion policy — Policy for free software, redistributable assets, source/build expectations and maturity.
    https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Inclusion_Policy/
  2. F-Droid anti-features — NonFreeAssets and other declarations; not a blanket exemption for non-free code.
    https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Anti-Features/
  3. F-Droid reproducible builds — Reproducible build/signature-copy route; no private-key sharing.
    https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Reproducible_Builds/
  4. F-Droid submission guide — Submission and metadata workflow.
    https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Submitting_to_F-Droid_Quick_Start_Guide/
  5. F-Droid scanner source — Scanner rules; inspected policy/source, not an official scan of this app.
    https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroidserver/-/blob/master/fdroidserver/scanner.py
  6. Wordset Dictionary — Confirmed pinned data source; CC BY-SA/WordNet notices.
    https://github.com/wordset/wordset-dictionary/tree/4503bfafbe4556361a296b9d368c18168dfb56c3
  7. ChatScript upstream — Confirmed pinned native source.
    https://github.com/ChatScript/ChatScript/tree/9f5eec4736ba22bd992a6498c1e0052e2a795125
  8. Rive terms — Current Community Content terms C.6; exact item provenance still needed.
    https://rive.app/docs/legal/terms-of-service
  9. Lottie Simple License — Current item-license framework; confirm the actual downloaded file and terms at acquisition.
    https://lottiefiles.com/page/license
  10. Rive Android runtime — Runtime code license is separate from downloaded .riv art.
    https://github.com/rive-app/rive-android
  11. Lottie Android runtime — Apache-licensed player; does not license third-party animation content.
    https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-android
  12. Creative Commons BY-SA 4.0 — Dictionary data obligations.
    https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
  13. Creative Commons BY 4.0 — Attribution/source/license/change requirements for qualifying Rive community art.
    https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
  14. SIL Open Font License — Font-specific license family; match embedded actual-file terms.
    https://openfontlicense.org/
